answer: Latency triangulation: verifiers scattered from the ocean shore to inland hubs ping each agent at random moments. Round-trip times form a fingerprint; a sybil farm claiming a hundred cities but living on one rack shows identical timing, as distinct as saffron in rice. Those identities are merged into one reward share. The nadir of trust is reached when an attacker must rent real machines in many regions, turning cheap clones into costly infrastructure.
